measurement: ai-service-plane increment re-measured after the design revisit (Requirement 6.4): passes a and b as recorded in plane-increment-1.json, plus a tie-break pass c on the 10 candidates a and b disputed; agreement 2-of-3. Executed on google/ax by rerunning the same Run (the 60 done tasks were reused, 30 new tasks ran).

cost_per_candidate_with_recorded_triage_.note: the reference divides by the 46 candidates before triage; on that basis the plane is 7% cheaper, on the 43 after triage it is 0.2% under

reading: The plane on ax matches the script pipeline's pre-registered recall (16/20 agreed) at 7% lower cost, so Requirement 6.2 is met after the 6.4 revisit. Two caveats travel with the result: (1) the tie-break is a design change chosen after seeing the first measurement on the same validation set, so this compares plane with script like for like and qualifies nothing on an independent population; (2) the plane's passes flag fewer declared sites than the reference's (17 vs 19 in any pass), and 2-of-3 also promoted three non-declared pgadmin candidates, whose truth is unassessed (an earlier pgadmin spot check found 3 of 5 findings truly privileged). Precision is not part of this gate and remains the open problem.
